preamble: Insertion of the near-open front vowel [æ] is attested in the history of Persian, where Middle Persian word-initial clusters of a consonant plus r were broken up by an anaptyctic vowel in New Persian. In Iranian Persian that vowel is the short /a/, realized [æ], so Middle Persian brād(ar) 'brother' surfaces as barādar [bæɾɒːˈdæɾ]. The same repair still splits consonant clusters in loanwords.

examples.note: An anaptyctic [æ] breaks the inherited initial cluster br-; Dari and Tajik have [a] in the same slot.
The initial cluster fr- is split by [æ].
The same anaptyxis before r applies; modern Persian phonotactics allow only a single onset consonant, and an epenthetic /a/~/æ/ also splits clusters in loanwords.
